name: Sansera Engineering Ltd
title: Sansera Engineering Ltd - 543358 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 revenue record INR 9,987m (+28% YoY) and EBITDA margin 19.3%, but new order booking soft and capex held at ~INR 5,097m for FY27 with forging capacity the binding constraint.

summary.headline: Sansera Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR 9,987 million (+28% YoY) with EBITDA margin up to 19.3% on ADS mix; PAT +108% to INR 1,231 million.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarter, with revenue up 28% YoY to INR 9,987 million, led by the Auto ICE business, the Non-Auto business (+70.5%) and the Swedish subsidiary. EBITDA rose 52% to INR 1,929 million, with margin up about 306 bps to 19.3%, attributed to ADS product mix and operating leverage. Full-year FY26 revenue reached INR 34,979 million (+16%), PAT INR 3,269 million (+51%), and management guided to a similar growth trajectory in FY27 with caution on input inflation. Order inflows in the quarter were soft, mainly from international customers.

financial_highlights.change: +52% YoY; margin vs 16.3% in Q4 FY25
+108% YoY; vs 7.6% margin in Q4 FY25
+170% YoY; includes INR 172 million forex gain and INR 54 million interest income

financial_highlights.metric: Operating cash flow net of tax (FY26)
financial_highlights.change: 11% of operating revenue (vs 12% last year); 61% of EBITDA

segments.name: Auto ICE
segments.commentary: Record quarterly revenue of INR 6,426 million, +21.6% YoY, driven by passenger vehicles (broad-based across OEMs) and commercial vehicles via the Swedish subsidiary.

segments.name: Auto Tech-Agnostic and xEV
segments.commentary: Record quarterly revenue of INR 1,217 million, +19.8% YoY.

segments.name: Non-Auto (incl. ADS)
segments.commentary: Record revenue of INR 1,736 million, +70.5% YoY; ADS business more than doubled YoY. ADS product sales for FY26 were INR 3,155 million (+155%), or about INR 3,498 million including scrap.

guidance_outlook: ADS FY27 revenue guided at about INR 550-600 crore, with the current order book executing to roughly INR 600 crore plus/minus; new building to contribute from Q3-Q4 FY27 and margins expected to move toward 25-30% as the facility fills.
Management expects a similar level of capex in FY27 as FY26 (INR 5,097 million), and confidence of sustaining a similar growth trajectory with healthy profitability.
Auto H1 FY27 expected to be relatively stronger than H2, aided by favorable base effect.
Order book visibility of around INR 8,000-8,200 crore toward the end of the decade, with a path to INR 10,000 crore over a couple of years, timing dependent on macro conditions.
Non-auto mix target of 20% may go above 20%; non-auto plus xEV/tech-agnostic was 30% for FY26 and 32% in Q4.
Nichidai JV facility machinery installation expected around September 2026; target to be operational around Q3 FY27; Sansera's JV contribution about INR 50 crore this year.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR 5,097 million; similar level expected in FY27, split between ICE capability expansion (existing facilities at maximum peak utilization) and new ADS facilities.
Incremental ADS capex of about INR 250 crore to clear the INR 4,500 crore current order backlog by 2031; ADS asset turn about 1:2.
Board approved acquisition of about 10 acres near the international airport, close to the aerospace park.

New Pantnagar facility inaugurated in FY26; building expansion expected to complete July-August 2026. Pantnagar second plant focused on 2-wheeler expansion; new long-term lease in Manesar for PV and 2-wheeler components; Pune expansion planned in FY27.

Forging capacity expansion at Plant 6 and machining at Plant 12 ongoing; forging output about 120 million components in FY26 with ~40% increase needed in the next couple of years. New lines are about 80% automated, with 20% manning.
Semicon machining constrained by mother machine lead times of 7-9 months; priority deliveries secured from DMG Mori, Yamazaki and Makino.
demand_pricing: Q4 new order booking was soft, largely from international customers due to global uncertainty; peak annual revenue for new business stands at INR 19.2 billion after annual reset; 5-year cumulative unexecuted lifetime order backlog INR 44.6 billion, especially ADS.

Aerospace: wallet-share gains on A350 and 737 platforms; new Boeing parts and a large engine maker win including a full blisk machining award (delivery in about 2 months). Semicon: ramped into mass production from end Q2 FY26 with volume surge; content value rising.
Exports: US EV customers had a weak year; management expects better export offtake, with order conversion taking 1-2 more quarters. US plant discussions restarted after a 10% tariff indication.
Two-wheeler: management says Sansera grew 29.9% YoY at Bajaj, 13.3% at TVS in Q4; outsourcing opportunities from in-sourcing OEMs (crankshaft assembly) expected to convert in FY27.
Passenger vehicles: stalled programs in North America and Europe restarting; domestic PV volumes expanding for Maruti and Tata Motors.
Energy storage program for a North American customer expected to add INR 80-100 crore annual revenue.
Content per vehicle target INR 5,000-10,000 for domestic ICE/hybrid; US connecting rod opportunity sized at 2-3 million rods per customer per year for Ford, Stellantis, GM programs (per management).
Input cost inflation in steel, aluminium, energy, tooling, consumables and freight; logistics costs and other expenses rose 28% YoY; labour availability is a constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Strategic roadmap for the next 2-4 years, with ADS at INR 1,300-1,400 crore and company revenue at INR 8,000-9,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the 60:40 auto ICE to non-auto/xEV mix goal, now at about 30% for FY26 and 32% in Q4; order book visibility of INR 8,000-8,200 crore toward the decade end, with INR 10,000 crore possible in a couple of years depending on macro conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Will ADS margins move toward 25-30% once the facility is fully utilised, and will more ADS capex follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins should move toward that range as the facility fills and the new building adds revenue in Q3-Q4 FY27. Incremental capex of about INR 250 crore is planned to clear the INR 4,500 crore backlog by 2031, with a 10-acre land purchase approved.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a one-time inventory refill in the non-auto US exports after tariffs eased?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-time refill; management expects better export offtake going forward, but order inflows will take one to two quarters to convert. US plant talks have restarted with more energy.

qa_highlights.question: Why does Sansera's two-wheeler growth lag Bajaj and TVS volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Sansera reports revenue, not units, and that it grew 29.9% at Bajaj and 13.3% at TVS in Q4, outgrowing the market; it is pursuing more share and outsourcing from key customers.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital pressure from ADS growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Auto working capital improved on inventory and receivables. ADS built a new working capital base, cutting operating cash conversion to 11% from 12%; localisation of raw material sources in semicon should shorten holding periods.

qa_highlights.question: Labour and inflation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Skilled and semi-skilled labour availability is a key execution challenge; the company is automating, raising women employees (about 65-70% at Pantnagar second plant) and using skill-based incentives.

risks_watch: Mother machine lead times of 7-9 months could constrain ADS and semicon ramp-up.
Forging capacity must grow about 40% in the next couple of years; long lead time for capex approval.
Input cost inflation (steel, aluminium, energy, freight) and labour availability/attrition.
Soft international order inflows and geopolitical or tariff volatility affecting US and European demand.
Working capital intensity rising with ADS; monitor operating cash flow conversion (11% of revenue in FY26).
Nichidai JV ramp (machinery installation about September 2026; operations targeted Q3 FY27) and MMRFIC investment (stake expected to be 45-50%).
Board changes: three new independent directors subject to shareholder approval; two directors retiring effective 27 July 2026.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term ADS and non-auto growth and order visibility, but explicitly cautious on FY27 macro, input inflation and order inflow conversion; several answers were qualified as dependent on macro conditions.
key_quotes: So as we go towards the end of this decade, we already have a visibility of closer to, as you said, about INR 8,000 crores, INR 8,200 crores on the order book front for the execution.
We are proceeding towards FY '27 with caution.
New order booking for the quarter remained soft, largely from international customers due to global uncertainty.
And we are already seeing that this needs to be 40% increase has to happen in the next couple of years.

growth.why: Management guides ADS FY27 revenue of about INR 550-600 crore with order book ~INR 600 crore and new building contributing from Q3-Q4 FY27, and expects a similar growth trajectory in FY27 on FY26 capex of INR 5,097 million; Q4 order inflows were soft, so backing is partial rather than fully contracted.
